title: 16. The Magic Art of the Great Humbug

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow told his friends, "Congratulations! I'm heading to Oz to get my brains today. When I return, I'll be just like everyone else."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人对朋友们说：“恭喜！我今天要去奥兹国取我的智慧。等我回来，我就和大家一样了。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy replied simply, "I've always liked you as you are." The Scarecrow said goodbye cheerfully and went to the Throne Room.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西简单地回答：“我一直喜欢你这个样子。”稻草人高兴地道了声再见，然后前往王宫大厅。

paragraphs.en: Oz greeted him: "Come in." Inside, Oz was deep in thought by the window.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹热情地迎接他：“请进。”此时，奥兹正靠在窗边陷入深思。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow explained, "I'm here for my brains."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人解释说：“我到这里来是为了获得智慧。”

paragraphs.en: Oz replied, "Sit down. I'll need to take your head off to put your new brains in place."
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹回答道：“坐下来。我得先把你脑袋摘下来，才能给你安上新的大脑。”

paragraphs.en: Oz removed the straw and filled the Scarecrow's head with a mixture of bran, pins, and needles. He then reattached the head, saying, "You will be wise from now on."
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹移开稻草，将燕麦壳、大头针和缝衣针的混合物填入稻草人的脑袋里，然后重新固定好脑袋，说道：“从现在起，你就会变得聪明了。”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow was pleased and thanked Oz before returning to his friends. Dorothy noticed his bulging head and asked, "How do you feel?"
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人感到很高兴，向奥兹表示感谢后，回到了朋友们中间。多萝西注意到他的头鼓了起来，问道：“你感觉怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: "Very wise," he replied earnestly. "Soon I'll know everything."
paragraphs.zh: “非常明智，”他认真地说，“很快我就什么都知道了。”

paragraphs.en: "Why are those needles sticking out?" the Tin Woodman inquired.
paragraphs.zh: “那些针为什么戳出来啦？”铁皮木人问道。

paragraphs.en: "The proof that I'm sharp," remarked the Lion.
The Tin Woodman then went to Oz for his heart. Knocking on the door, he said, "I've come for my heart."
paragraphs.zh: 随后，锡人前往奥兹国取回他的心。他敲了敲门，说道：“我来拿我的心。”

paragraphs.en: Oz said he would need to cut a small hole in the Tin Woodman's breast to place a silk heart filled with sawdust. The Woodman assured him it wouldn't hurt. Oz made the incision, inserted the heart, and sealed the wound.
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹说他需要在铁皮人胸口开一个小孔，放入一个装满锯末的丝绸心脏。铁皮人保证这不会疼。奥兹做了切割，植入了心脏，并缝合了伤口。

paragraphs.en: The Woodman expressed gratitude for his new heart, though he wondered if it was kind. Oz confirmed it was very kind. The Woodman rejoined his friends, who congratulated him on his good fortune.
paragraphs.zh: 伐木工对新得到的心脏表示感激，尽管他怀疑这种恩赐是否出于好意。奥兹确认这确实是一份非常慷慨的礼物。于是，伐木工重新加入了他的朋友们，大家纷纷向他表示祝贺，为他的好运感到高兴。

paragraphs.en: Next, the Lion approached the Throne Room. Oz agreed to give him courage. He retrieved a green bottle from a high shelf and poured its contents into a carved dish.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，狮子走向了王座室。奥兹同意给他勇气。他从高高的架子上取下一个绿瓶，将里面的液体倒入了一个雕刻精美的盘子里。

paragraphs.en: The Lion hesitated but drank until the dish was empty. Oz asked how he felt. The Lion replied that he now felt full of courage, returning to his friends with this good news.
paragraphs.zh: 狮子犹豫了一下，但还是把盘子里的东西都喝了下去。奥兹问他感觉怎么样。狮子回答说，现在他感到充满了勇气，带着这个好消息回到朋友们中间。

paragraphs.en: Oz reflected on his success in granting the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion what they believed they desired. "How can I help being a humbug?" he mused, "when everyone expects me to perform impossible feats?"
paragraphs.zh: 奥兹思索着自己如何能让稻草人、铁皮人和狮子得到了他们以为想要的东西。“我怎么能不装神弄鬼呢？”他自言自语道，“大家不是都指望我能完成那些不可能的任务吗？”

paragraphs.en: It was simple to please them since they thought he could do anything. However, returning Dorothy to Kansas would require more than imagination, and Oz admitted he had no idea how it could be accomplished.
paragraphs.zh: 让他们高兴起来很简单，因为他们认为他无所不能。然而，要把多萝西送回堪萨斯州可不仅仅靠想象，奥兹承认自己也不知道该如何实现这个愿望。
